findings.title: MetricsMiddleware shares mutable `next` field across all wrapped clients, causing data race and cross-request client confusion
findings.body: NewMetricsMiddleware creates a single *MetricsMiddleware instance (`imw`) and then mutates its `next` field inside the ClientMiddlewareFunc closure: `imw.next = next; return imw`. Because the same `imw` pointer is returned for every invocation of the middleware function, all plugin clients wrapped by this middleware share the same `next` field. The middleware factory is invoked once per plugin client (per plugin/process), so the last client to be wrapped overwrites `next` for all previously wrapped clients. This is a data race if clients are created concurrently, and even when created sequentially it means every wrapped client will call whichever `next` was assigned last — requests for plugin A will be forwarded to plugin B's client. The consequence is that plugin requests are routed to the wrong plugin backend (data integrity/security issue: queries for one data source can be sent to another plugin), and concurrent client construction triggers the Go race detector. The correct pattern (used by the other middlewares in this package, e.g. LoggerMiddleware and ContextualLoggerMiddleware) is to construct a new middleware struct per invocation: `return &MetricsMiddleware{pluginMetrics: ..., pluginRegistry: ..., next: next}`. The metrics registration part (newMetricsMiddleware) can stay shared, but the per-client state must not be.

findings.title: Logger name 'plugin.instrumentation' no longer matches the renamed middleware
findings.body: The logger middleware is still constructed with the logger name `log.New("plugin.instrumentation")` even though the instrumentation middleware was renamed to metrics middleware and the contextual logging was moved out of it. The logger name should be updated (e.g. `plugin.metrics` or similar) to reflect the actual component, otherwise log filtering/queries by logger name will be misleading. This is a leftover from the rename.

findings.title: ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add contextual attributes for SubscribeStream, PublishStream, and RunStream
findings.body: The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware only calls instrumentContext (which adds endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname contextual log attributes) for QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, and CollectMetrics. For SubscribeStream, PublishStream, and RunStream it passes the context through unchanged. Previously (in the old InstrumentationMiddleware) the same three streaming methods also did not instrument the context, so this is not a regression, but it means streaming plugin requests will lack the contextual logger attributes that the PR description says were moved to the LoggerMiddleware. If the intent is for all plugin requests to have contextual logging, these three methods should also call instrumentContext with the appropriate endpoint constant. At minimum this inconsistency should be a conscious decision; as written, log lines emitted during streaming requests will be missing pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname fields.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware now depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware ordering but drops traceID from log output
findings.body: The logRequest method previously appended `traceID` (from tracing.TraceIDFromContext) to the log params; that code was removed in this PR. The traceID is still recorded as a Prometheus exemplar in MetricsMiddleware, but it is no longer present in the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line. Correlating a log line with a trace (and with the exemplar-bearing metrics) now requires joining on other fields. If dropping traceID from logs was intentional it should be called out; otherwise it is a regression in observability. Additionally, the logger now relies on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` picking up contextual attributes that are only present if ContextualLoggerMiddleware runs earlier in the chain (it does in pluginsintegration.go), but LoggerMiddleware itself has no guard or documentation that it must be placed after ContextualLoggerMiddleware — if the ordering is ever changed, the pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname fields silently disappear from these log lines.

findings.title: FromContext silently discards the receiver's existing context when the context logger is not a *log.ConcreteLogger
findings.body: grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext calls d.l.FromContext(ctx) and type-asserts the result to *log.ConcreteLogger. If the assertion fails it returns d.New() — a logger with only the receiver's own base context — completely ignoring the contextual attributes stored in the provided ctx. This means that whenever the logger stored in the context is not the concrete infra logger type (e.g. a wrapped logger, a logger from a different package, or a logger created via log.New with a different wrapper), all contextual attributes (pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, uname, traceID, etc.) are silently dropped. The method should fall back to something that preserves the context-derived logger, e.g. return a wrapper around d.l.FromContext(ctx) result without the type assertion, or at minimum document the limitation. As written, the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware + LoggerMiddleware combination can silently lose all contextual log fields depending on which logger implementation ends up in the context.
